title: verification-result
description: The verifier stage's verdict. The coordinator routes the workflow on status and retry_recommended, so both are required.

status.description: The verdict the coordinator routes on.

severity.description: How badly the finding blocks acceptance.

location.description: File or area the finding applies to.

required_behavior.description: What must be true for the finding to clear.

unverified.description: What could not be verified, and why.

retry_recommended.description: Whether the coordinator should route a bounded retry.

retry_target.description: The retry category the next attempt is routed on, named exactly as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. The coordinator requires it whenever retry_recommended is true, and escalates on a missing or unrecognised one rather than falling back to a default route. It is not in required because this schema cannot express that condition: the validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so 'required when retry_recommended is true' is inexpressible, and requiring it unconditionally would force a routing key onto a passing verification that routes nowhere.

guidance_outcomes.description: One object per entry of the retry guidance in force for the attempt this verdict judges: every current_focus focus and every preserve_behavior string of it, each echoed verbatim and answered. Every entry must be accounted for, so a retry that regressed behaviour it was told to preserve fails normally rather than reading as defective guidance. The coordinator compares the echoed set against the guidance in force it recorded when the retry was routed, and escalates on any mismatch — missing, extra, misquoted or absent altogether — rather than assuming what silence meant. When every entry is accounted for and none is unmet, a failed verdict is a contradiction: the guidance sanctioned the outcome it is being failed for, and the verifier runs again in place to rewrite guidance that does not authorize what it will fail, or to fail the work on the criterion it actually failed. It is optional because a first verification has no guidance in force to answer.

guidance.description: One entry of the guidance in force, echoed verbatim: a current_focus focus or a preserve_behavior string, character for character as the guidance carries it. The coordinator compares strings and reads none of them as language, so a paraphrase is a mismatch.

unmet.description: Why this entry was not met. Its presence is the signal that the retry did not meet the entry, and its content is the reason. It is one string rather than a boolean with a sibling reason for the same limitation retry_target and unfinishable_by_retry record: this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so 'reason required when the flag is true' is inexpressible, and a flag with a sibling reason has a state where the flag is set and the reason is missing, while presence-as-signal has none. Judge the entry against the satisfied_when written when the entry was written, not against a condition arrived at now. Absent means the entry was met.

correctable_findings.description: Findings you judge correct but too small to fail the run, that one stage can fix mechanically. Its presence is the signal that a correction pass should run: there is no separate key saying whether this field means anything, for the same limitation retry_target, unfinishable_by_retry and guidance_outcomes.unmet already record above — this validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so a flag with a sibling payload has a state where the flag is set and the payload is missing, while presence-as-signal has none. A correctable finding is a correction to words alone — a comment, a docstring, a schema description, a document — and never to behaviour: nothing a correction pass changes may alter what any test asserts about the system, and the suite must pass unchanged across a pass. A finding whose repair would change behaviour is a blocking issue or belongs in unverified, not here. It is read only on a passing verdict, because a failed verdict already routes and the correction travels in the retry guidance it already writes. It is optional because almost every verdict has no such finding.

location.description: Where the wording is: the file, and the symbol, section or line within it that carries the words to correct.

finding.description: What is wrong with the words as they stand.

correction.description: What the words should say instead, specifically enough that a stage can make the edit without re-deciding what the finding meant.

category.description: The retry category that owns the prose being corrected, spelled exactly as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. The field introduces no new vocabulary: the coordinator reads the destination off that same table, so a category the workflow does not declare escalates the run naming the categories it does, with the same strictness an unrecognised retry_target gets.

unfinishable_by_retry.description: The verifier's judgement that no number of retries closes the gap between what remains and what an attempt delivers, together with the split it recommends between this story and a follow-on. Its presence on a failed verdict ends the run in escalation at that verification, before the retry count is compared to the ceiling: the budget is left unspent and the retry count untouched, because the judgement is that spending them would not finish the work. Its content is both the judgement and the escalation's recorded reason, so the developer reads the verifier's own words rather than a reason the coordinator composed. It is one string rather than a boolean with a sibling reason for the same limitation retry_target records above: the validator subset has no if/then and no dependentRequired, so 'reason required when the flag is true' is inexpressible, and presence-as-signal leaves no state where the signal is set and the reason is missing. It is optional because almost every verdict has no such judgement to make, and it is read only on a failed verdict — a passing verification routes nowhere, so nothing there could act on it.
